stem: What is the accounting equation?
options: Assets = Liabilities + Equity
Assets = Revenue - Expenses
Equity = Assets + Liabilities + Revenue
Revenue = Assets - Equity
explanation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

stem: In double-entry bookkeeping, a company pays rent in cash. What happens?
options: Debit rent expense and credit cash in day-to-day work
Debit cash and credit rent expense
Debit rent expense and credit equity
Credit rent expense and credit cash
explanation: Debit rent expense and credit cash.

stem: A company delivers services in December but is paid in January. Under accrual accounting, when is the revenue recorded?
options: In December, when the service is delivered
In January, when the cash is finally received
Spread evenly over both months in most cases
When the invoice is archived in day-to-day work
explanation: In December, when it is earned.

stem: A trial balance does not balance by IDR 500,000. What is the best first step?
options: Look for a one-sided entry or a posting error
Add 500,000 to the cash account
Delete the last month of entries
Round most of the totals to the nearest million rupiah
explanation: Check for a posting error, such as a transposition, a one-sided entry or a wrong amount.

stem: Equipment bought for IDR 120 million is used for 4 years with no residual value. What is the yearly straight-line depreciation?
options: IDR 30 million
IDR 40 million
IDR 24 million
IDR 60 million
explanation: 120 million / 4 = 30 million per year.

stem: Which of these is an accounting software widely used by Indonesian SMEs?
options: Accurate
Photoshop
AutoCAD
Premiere
explanation: Accurate (also Jurnal, Zahir).

stem: What is a chart of accounts?
options: The list of accounts used to classify transactions
A graph of monthly sales
A table of the staff and their salaries at that stage
A schedule of tax deadlines
explanation: The list of all accounts used to classify transactions.

stem: A sales invoice is entered in accounting software. Which entries are posted automatically?
options: Debit receivables, credit sales and output VAT
Debit sales, credit cash and equity
Debit inventory, credit payables and VAT
Debit expenses, credit sales and receivables together
explanation: Receivable (and VAT, revenue) are posted; typically debit accounts receivable, credit sales and output VAT.

stem: In SAP, which module covers financial accounting and controlling?
options: FICO
MM
SD
HCM
explanation: SAP FICO.

stem: Why should period locking be used in accounting software after closing?
options: To stop changes to closed periods and keep reports stable
To make the software run faster at month end in practice as the work grows
To hide the transactions from auditors
To remove old customers from the system
explanation: To prevent changes to closed periods and keep reported numbers stable.

stem: What does accounts payable represent?
options: Money the company owes to suppliers
Money that customers owe to the company
Money that is held in the bank account
Money paid to staff as salary
explanation: Money the company owes to suppliers.

stem: What does a bank reconciliation compare?
options: The cash book with the bank statement
The budget with the forecast for the business
The invoice with the original purchase request
The payroll with the tax return during the project
explanation: The company's cash book with the bank statement.

stem: Three-way matching compares which documents before paying a supplier?
options: Purchase order, goods receipt and invoice
Quotation, contract and the payment slip in practice
Invoice, bank statement and the annual tax return
Budget, order and delivery schedule for the project
explanation: Purchase order, goods receipt and supplier invoice.

stem: An aged receivables report shows many invoices older than 90 days. What should the team do?
options: Follow up collections and assess a doubtful-debt provision
Delete the invoices from the ledger
Record them as revenue for the next year from the start in the long run
Offer a larger discount on new orders in a real project in many setups
explanation: Follow up on collections and assess the need for a provision for doubtful debts.

stem: The bank statement shows a deposit of IDR 5 million that is not in the cash book. What is the correct treatment?
options: Investigate it and record it in the cash book
Ignore it until the next audit
Reduce the bank balance in the books by the same amount
Record it as an expense of the month in a real project
explanation: Investigate and record it in the cash book (for example a customer transfer) so both agree.

stem: What is the purpose of internal control?
options: Safeguard assets and ensure reliable reporting
Increase the sales of the company
Reduce the number of employees
Replace the external audit
explanation: To safeguard assets, ensure reliable reporting and encourage compliance.

stem: What is segregation of duties?
options: Splitting authorising, recording and custody between people
Giving one person control of the whole process at that stage
Rotating staff between offices each year in practice within the team
Keeping each department in a separate building from the start
explanation: Splitting tasks such as authorising, recording and custody between different people.

stem: Which is a preventive control?
options: An approval limit before a payment is made for the project
A monthly review of the bank statements by a manager
An audit after the year end
A report of last quarter's errors
explanation: Approval limits that stop a payment before it is made.

stem: What is audit sampling?
options: Testing a selection and concluding about the whole population
Checking each single transaction of the year in many setups in many setups
Asking the management to pick the evidence
Reviewing just the largest customer
explanation: Testing a selected portion of items and drawing conclusions about the whole population.

stem: An auditor finds that the same employee creates vendors and approves their payments. What is this?
options: A segregation-of-duties weakness and fraud risk
A normal efficiency in a small company at that stage
A strength of the purchasing process
A timing difference in the ledger
explanation: A segregation of duties weakness and a fraud risk.

stem: What is a budget?
options: A plan of expected income and spending from the start for the project
A report of past income and spending
A list of the customers of the company and their orders
A record of the assets of the company
explanation: A plan of expected income and spending for a future period.

stem: What does a rolling forecast do?
options: It is updated regularly and always looks ahead a fixed time
It is fixed once a year and rarely changed for the business in the long run
It records just what has already happened
It is written by the auditors
explanation: It is updated regularly and always looks a fixed number of periods ahead.

stem: What is the difference between CAPEX and OPEX?
options: CAPEX buys long-term assets, OPEX covers running costs within the team
CAPEX covers running costs, while OPEX buys long-term assets
CAPEX is for taxes, OPEX is for salaries
They are two names for the same cost
explanation: CAPEX buys long-term assets; OPEX covers day-to-day running costs.

stem: A project costs IDR 100 million and returns IDR 40 million a year. What is the payback period?
options: 2.5 years
4 years
40 months
1.5 years

stem: In a DCF valuation, a higher discount rate does what to present value?
options: Lowers the present value
Raises the present value
Leaves it unchanged
Turns it negative in all cases
explanation: It lowers the present value of future cash flows.

stem: Which cost stays the same regardless of production volume in the short run?
options: A fixed cost such as rent during the project
A variable cost such as raw materials in day-to-day work
A direct cost such as sales commission in most cases
A mixed cost such as electricity
explanation: A fixed cost, such as rent.

stem: What does COGS stand for?
options: Cost of goods sold
Cash on goods and services
Cost of general supplies
Capital of group subsidiaries
explanation: Cost of goods sold (HPP).

stem: Fixed costs are IDR 60 million, the selling price is IDR 50,000 and the variable cost is IDR 20,000 per unit. What is the break-even volume?
options: 2,000 units
1,200 units
3,000 units
1,500 units

stem: Purchases are 10 units at 100, then 10 units at 120. Under FIFO, what is the cost of the first 10 units sold?
explanation: FIFO uses the oldest costs first: 10 x 100 = 1,000.

stem: Prices of materials are rising. Which inventory costing method reports the highest profit?
options: FIFO, which expenses the oldest costs first
Weighted average, which blends most the costs
Specific identification of each of the units that were sold
The method does not change the profit as the work grows
explanation: FIFO expenses the oldest, lower costs first, so COGS is lower and profit higher when prices rise.

stem: Which statement reports revenues and expenses over a period?
options: Income statement
Balance sheet
Cash flow statement
Statement of changes in equity
explanation: The income statement (profit and loss).

stem: Which statement shows assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time?
options: Balance sheet
Income statement
Cash flow statement
Trial balance alone
explanation: The balance sheet.

stem: A company is profitable but has little cash. Which statement explains why?
options: The cash flow statement
The income statement
The chart of accounts
The trial balance
explanation: The cash flow statement, which shows operating, investing and financing cash movements.

stem: What is the purpose of month-end closing?
options: Record adjustments and reconcile accounts to report the period
Delete the transactions of the previous month
Lock the accounts and stop all new sales
Print each invoice for the archive
explanation: To record accruals and adjustments, reconcile accounts and produce accurate reports for the period.

stem: Sales were IDR 800 million against a budget of IDR 900 million. What is the variance?
options: Unfavourable by IDR 100 million (11.1%)
Favourable by IDR 100 million (11.1%)
Unfavourable by IDR 100 million (12.5% of actual)
Favourable by IDR 90 million (10%)
explanation: Actual minus budget = -100 million: an unfavourable variance of 11.1%.

stem: Which Indonesian tax is withheld from employee salaries?
options: PPh 21
PPh 23
PPN
PBB
explanation: PPh 21.

stem: What is the general VAT (PPN) rate in Indonesia since April 2022 up to 2024?
explanation: 11% from 1 April 2022 (12% applies to luxury goods from 2025).

stem: Which tax is withheld on payments for services such as consulting or rent of assets other than land and buildings?
options: PPh 23
PPh 21
PPh 25
PPh Final 4(2)
explanation: PPh 23.

stem: What is the e-Faktur used for?
options: Issuing electronic VAT invoices in most cases in most cases
Paying the annual income tax of the company
Registering a new company name with the ministry
Filing a customs declaration
explanation: Issuing electronic VAT invoices (faktur pajak) for PKP taxable businesses.

stem: Input VAT of IDR 40 million and output VAT of IDR 55 million arise in a month. What is the result?
options: IDR 15 million VAT payable
IDR 15 million VAT refundable
IDR 95 million VAT payable
IDR 40 million VAT payable
explanation: Output minus input = 15 million VAT payable.
